### CVE-2019-0186
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2019-04-26 | Updated: 2024-08-04 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: Cross-Site Scripting
- Exploit-DB 46759: Apache Pluto 3.0.0 / 3.0.1 - Persistent Cross-Site Scripting (webapps/java, 2019-04-26, verified=0)

The input fields of the Apache Pluto "Chat Room" demo portlet 3.0.0 and 3.0.1 are vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. Mitigation: * Uninstall the ChatRoomDemo war file - or - * migrate to version 3.1.0 of the chat-room-demo war file

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Pluto: affected 3.0.0; affected 3.0.1

### CVE-2019-0193
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2019-08-01 | Updated: 2025-10-21 | Max CVSS: 7.2
- CWE: Information Disclosure; CWE-94 CWE-94 Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2021-12-10, ransomware=Unknown — Apache Solr DataImportHandler Code Injection Vulnerability

In Apache Solr, the DataImportHandler, an optional but popular module to pull in data from databases and other sources, has a feature in which the whole DIH configuration can come from a request's "dataConfig" parameter. The debug mode of the DIH admin screen uses this to allow convenient debugging / development of a DIH config. Since a DIH config can contain scripts, this parameter is a security risk. Starting with version 8.2.0 of Solr, use of this parameter requires setting the Java System property "enable.dih.dataConfigParam" to true.

Affected:
- Apache / Apache Solr: affected Apache Solr all prior to 8.2.0

### CVE-2019-0211
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2019-04-08 | Updated: 2025-10-21 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: Apache HTTP Server privilege escalation from modules' scripts; CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free

- **CISA KEV**: added 2021-11-03, ransomware=Unknown — Apache HTTP Server Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
- Exploit-DB 46676: Apache 2.4.17 < 2.4.38 - 'apache2ctl graceful' 'logrotate' Local Privilege Escalation (local/linux, 2019-04-08, verified=0)

In Apache HTTP Server 2.4 releases 2.4.17 to 2.4.38, with MPM event, worker or prefork, code executing in less-privileged child processes or threads (including scripts executed by an in-process scripting interpreter) could execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the parent process (usually root) by manipulating the scoreboard. Non-Unix systems are not affected.

Affected:
- Apache / Apache HTTP Server: affected 2.4.17 to 2.4.38

### CVE-2019-0221
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2019-05-28 | Updated: 2026-11-02 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: Cross-Site Scripting
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial
- Exploit-DB 50119: Apache Tomcat 9.0.0.M1 - Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (webapps/multiple, 2021-07-13, verified=0)

The SSI printenv command in Apache Tomcat 9.0.0.M1 to 9.0.0.17, 8.5.0 to 8.5.39 and 7.0.0 to 7.0.93 echoes user provided data without escaping and is, therefore, vulnerable to XSS. SSI is disabled by default. The printenv command is intended for debugging and is unlikely to be present in a production website.

Affected:
- Apache / Apache Tomcat: affected Apache Tomcat 9.0.0.M1 to 9.0.0.17; affected 8.5.0 to 8.5.39; affected 7.0.0 to 7.0.93

### CVE-2019-0232
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2019-04-15 | Updated: 2026-11-02 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: Remote Code Execution
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- Exploit-DB 47073: Apache Tomcat - CGIServlet enableCmdLineArguments Remote Code Execution (Metasploit) (remote/windows, 2019-07-03, verified=1)

When running on Windows with enableCmdLineArguments enabled, the CGI Servlet in Apache Tomcat 9.0.0.M1 to 9.0.17, 8.5.0 to 8.5.39 and 7.0.0 to 7.0.93 is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution due to a bug in the way the JRE passes command line arguments to Windows. The CGI Servlet is disabled by default. The CGI option enableCmdLineArguments is disable by default in Tomcat 9.0.x (and will be disabled by default in all versions in response to this vulnerability). For a detailed explanation of the JRE behaviour, see Markus Wulftange's blog (https://codewhitesec.blogspot.com/2016/02/java-and-command-line-injections-in-windows.html) and this archived MSDN blog (https://web.archive.org/web/20161228144344/https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/twistylittlepassagesallalike/2011/04/23/everyone-quotes-command-line-arguments-the-wrong-way/).

Affected:
- Apache / Tomcat: affected 9.0.0.M1 to 9.0.17; affected 8.5.0 to 8.5.39; affected 7.0.0 to 7.0.93

### CVE-2019-10092
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2019-09-26 | Updated: 2024-08-04 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: Limited cross-site scriptingcross-site scripting in mod_proxy
- Exploit-DB 47688: Apache Httpd mod_proxy - Error Page Cross-Site Scripting (webapps/multiple, 2019-10-14, verified=0)

In Apache HTTP Server 2.4.0-2.4.39, a limited cross-site scripting issue was reported affecting the mod_proxy error page. An attacker could cause the link on the error page to be malformed and instead point to a page of their choice. This would only be exploitable where a server was set up with proxying enabled but was misconfigured in such a way that the Proxy Error page was displayed.

Affected:
- n/a / Apache HTTP Server: affected 2.4.0 to 2.4.39

### CVE-2019-17558
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2019-12-30 | Updated: 2025-10-21 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: Information Disclosure; CWE-74 CWE-74 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2021-11-03, ransomware=Unknown — Apache Solr VelocityResponseWriter Plug-In Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
- Exploit-DB 47572: Apache Solr 8.2.0 - Remote Code Execution (webapps/java, 2019-11-01, verified=0)
- Exploit-DB 48338: Apache Solr - Remote Code Execution via Velocity Template (Metasploit) (remote/multiple, 2020-04-16, verified=1)

Apache Solr 5.0.0 to Apache Solr 8.3.1 are vulnerable to a Remote Code Execution through the VelocityResponseWriter. A Velocity template can be provided through Velocity templates in a configset `velocity/` directory or as a parameter. A user defined configset could contain renderable, potentially malicious, templates. Parameter provided templates are disabled by default, but can be enabled by setting `params.resource.loader.enabled` by defining a response writer with that setting set to `true`. Defining a response writer requires configuration API access. Solr 8.4 removed the params resource loader entirely, and only enables the configset-provided template rendering when the configset is `trusted` (has been uploaded by an authenticated user).

Affected:
- n/a / Apache Solr: affected Apache Solr 5.0.0 to Apache Solr 8.3.1

### CVE-2019-17571
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2019-12-20 | Updated: 2026-05-28 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-502 CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data; CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Included in Log4j 1.2 is a SocketServer class that is vulnerable to deserialization of untrusted data which can be exploited to remotely execute arbitrary code when combined with a deserialization gadget when listening to untrusted network traffic for log data. This affects Log4j versions up to 1.2 up to 1.2.17.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Log4j: affected versions up to 1.2.17

### CVE-2019-19791
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2023-05-29 | Updated: 2025-01-14 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: n/a; CWE-noinfo Not enough information
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

In LemonLDAP::NG (aka lemonldap-ng) before 2.0.7, the default Apache HTTP Server configuration does not properly restrict access to SOAP/REST endpoints (when some LemonLDAP::NG setup options are used). For example, an attacker can insert index.fcgi/index.fcgi into a URL to bypass a Require directive.

- n/a / n/a: affected n/a
